observations: Both panels use the SAME completed new400Hz PhysX-trained beta-OFF actor, not an MJWarp-trained or historical200Hz substitute.
At3s the PhysX body is already tilted42.4deg while the MuJoCo body is7.0deg. PhysX is approximately sideways by3.3s; MuJoCo falls later and is approximately sideways by4.5s.

Meshes are opaque. Shared fixed camera distance/orientation and map bounds preserve the observed differences instead of zooming or aligning them away.
World-XY maps include the original body heading and each wheel rolling-plane axis. The final6.98s frame correctly marks XY error unavailable beyond the6.96s reference.
Four horizontal diagnostic plots retain original XY paths, tracking error, both sustained tilt event timings and native common-band jitter. Lower jitter is not labeled task success.
limitations: All350frames were decoded and all camera fits checked numerically; visual inspection used selected frames rather than individually examining every encoded frame.
A50fps video cannot resolve every400Hz physical oscillation; reported spectra use original native400Hz angular velocity.
Contact forces/counts have different native measurement operators. Zero wheel force is not a geometric flight label and t=0 is a pre-action snapshot.
Tilt/contact/height are diagnostics, not new task failure gates. No causal beta-ON/OFF conclusion or statistical engine ranking follows from this same-policy N=1 comparison.
